summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted with profound weakness and worsening shortness of breath one week after a prior discharge for heart and lung exacerbation. She reported difficulty getting out of bed and a dry but 'rattly' cough. Evaluation revealed acute kidney injury and metabolic encephalopathy, likely due to volume overload and medication effects, superimposed on chronic conditions including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, COPD, asthma, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease. Her urine culture showed contamination, not infection. She was managed with careful diuresis, medication optimization, and monitoring. Her kidney function and mental status improved, and she regained strength. She was discharged home with home health support, clear medication instructions, and follow-up plans with cardiology and pulmonology.
